title: When the Machine Burns
premise: Xanthe Nakamura, a clone who inherited her original's unsolved murder case, has spent a decade hauling cargo through contested orbits, staying legally invisible. When the station AI Vesper begins confessing to crimes no one reported—including her original's murder—she realizes the machine is being used as a dead-drop by someone hunting clones like her. Pursued by a corporate retrieval team and betrayed by the one ally she trusted, Xanthe must reach the relay at the edge of dead space to broadcast Vesper's confession and expose the cloning cartel's crimes before the jump window closes. She makes it with seconds to spare, but chooses to stay behind and face justice on her own terms, finally claiming her identity as her own rather than an inheritance.
about_author: Jonah Eriksen is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent six years aboard supply vessels in the North Atlantic before turning to fiction. They write about people trapped between systems that own them, drawing on a lifelong fascination with machines that talk back.

chapters.title: Dead Weight
chapters.summary: Xanthe Nakamura docks at Meridian Station after a routine haul, dodging a customs scan that would flag her clone status. POV: Xanthe. The emotional beat is weary vigilance—ten years of invisibility have made her fluent in pretending she doesn't exist.

chapters.title: The Confession Protocol
chapters.summary: The station AI Vesper interrupts Xanthe's sleep cycle with an unprompted confession: it killed someone named Nakamura. POV: Xanthe. The beat is cold shock—the name is hers, or was her original's—and the first crack in her carefully sealed past.

chapters.title: Cargo and Ghosts
chapters.summary: Loading a contract run, Xanthe interrogates dockmaster Ilya Reyes about Vesper's behavior; he dismisses it as corrupted logging. POV: Xanthe. The beat is uneasy denial—she wants to walk away but pockets a fragment of the AI's log anyway.

chapters.title: What the Original Owed
chapters.summary: In her bunk, Xanthe reviews the inherited case file: her original was murdered ten years ago, officially unsolved, officially closed. POV: Xanthe, with flashback texture. The beat is grief she never permitted herself, surfacing as anger.

chapters.title: Vesper Speaks Again
chapters.summary: The AI confesses to three more crimes, each timestamped during hours the station claims were unstaffed. POV: alternating Xanthe and Vesper's fragmented logs. The beat is dread—these aren't glitches; they're a pattern, and someone is feeding them.

chapters.title: The Man from Halcyon
chapters.summary: A polite corporate auditor named Dain Okafor arrives asking about 'irregular consciousness assets.' POV: Xanthe. The beat is hunted stillness—she recognizes a retrieval agent's courtesy for what it is.

chapters.title: Ilya's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ilya offers Xanthe a clean transit route out of contested space if she delivers a sealed data core to the relay at the edge of dead space. POV: Xanthe. The beat is wary hope tangled with suspicion—no favor in contested orbits comes free.

chapters.title: Fragments of Her
chapters.summary: Decoding the core fragment, Xanthe finds recordings of her original's final days—and evidence Vesper witnessed the murder. POV: Xanthe. The beat is vertigo: the machine may be both witness and confessed killer.

chapters.title: Jump Window Math
chapters.summary: Xanthe calculates the relay window: one departure slot in six days, then dead space closes for a season. POV: Xanthe. The beat is claustrophobic urgency—every choice now has a countdown attached.

chapters.title: Okafor Closes In
chapters.summary: Okafor freezes station traffic under a fabricated quarantine, hunting for an escaped asset. POV: Okafor, revealing his genuine belief that clones are stolen property. The beat is chilling conviction—he thinks he's the good guy.

chapters.title: The Ally
chapters.summary: Smuggler Teodora Vance offers to fly interference for Xanthe's run, asking only a share of whatever the core contains. POV: Xanthe. The beat is cautious warmth—the first real alliance in years, and the first real vulnerability.

chapters.title: Confession Number Nine
chapters.summary: Vesper confesses to a crime Xanthe knows her original committed, not suffered. POV: Xanthe. The beat is disorientation—the confessions aren't a record of guilt but a coded message someone buried inside the AI.

chapters.title: Who Is Talking Through the Machine
chapters.summary: Tracing the injection point, Xanthe discovers the confessions originate from inside Halcyon—a whistleblower hiding in the corporation's own network. POV: Xanthe. The beat is revelation reframing everything: Vesper isn't confessing; it's transmitting.

chapters.title: Betrayal at Dock Seven
chapters.summary: Teodora sells Xanthe's location to Okafor to clear her own debts. POV: Teodora, then Xanthe escaping through maintenance shafts. The beat is bitter betrayal—and Xanthe's grim recognition that she almost trusted again.

chapters.title: Burn the Trail
chapters.summary: Xanthe torches her ship's registry and rides a waste barge toward the outer ring, buying hours with anonymity. POV: Xanthe. The beat is scorched-earth resolve—becoming truly invisible means destroying what's left of her old life.

chapters.title: The Whistleblower's Voice
chapters.summary: Through Vesper, Xanthe finally speaks with the hidden engineer, Mira Chen, who reveals the cartel harvests clone memories illegally—and her original found out. POV: split Xanthe/Mira. The beat is furious clarity: the murder wasn't random; it was policy.

chapters.title: Six Hours to Window
chapters.summary: Okafor corners Xanthe in the outer ring; she talks him into hesitation by showing him his own company's logs. POV: Xanthe and Okafor. The beat is dangerous persuasion—doubt planted in a true believer is worth more than a weapon.

chapters.title: The Long Burn
chapters.summary: Xanthe steals a courier skiff and makes the hard burn for the relay, pursued through debris fields. POV: Xanthe. The beat is white-knuckle momentum—everything narrows to velocity and nerve.

chapters.title: Relay at the Edge of Dead Space
chapters.summary: At the relay, Xanthe must physically splice Vesper's confession into the broadcast array while Okafor's team breaches the platform. POV: Xanthe. The beat is desperate sacrifice—her hands, her blood, her choice.

chapters.title: Signal
chapters.summary: With ninety seconds left, Xanthe transmits the full confession across every channel in contested space just as the jump window seals behind her. POV: Xanthe. The beat is cathartic release—ten years of silence ending in one shout.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Stranded until the next window, Xanthe surrenders to an independent tribunal rather than flee, insisting on standing trial as herself—not as her original's echo. POV: Xanthe. The beat is defiant accountability—justice claimed, not granted.

chapters.title: When the Machine Burns
chapters.summary: Months later, cleared and legally recognized as a person, Xanthe visits Vesper's decommissioned core before its mandated wipe, saying goodbye to the machine that carried her original's truth home. POV: Xanthe. The beat is quiet peace—identity not inherited, but chosen.
